blocks.text: Durable things (coins, a bag, XP) are player.state: back on every rejoin over the template, a dot write where the player simulates with no round trip and no save call; one tick's writes (no await between) save as one piece. Seed ONCE: player.state.run ??= {…} at the first arrival, never = … on a spawn, which throws the save away. A fresh start ("reset my progress", NEW GAME) is player.state = {} on their row (ctx.self.state = {} in their own behavior; a ctx.world.players row from sim.js or run_script): the save empties at once and the next join stamps the template. The engine saves where a player stands. sim.js referees a claim several hands make at once (the win, the last seat). SQL answers what only a table answers (every player ever, every room: the all-time board, a gift between players), rows keyed on userId. History grows forever: boards and totals read a running summary.

// the pickup: the chest's hook, where it simulates; the bag is the player's row export function onTriggerEnter(ctx, player) { if (!player.tags.includes("player")) return; player.state.bag ??= {}; player.state.bag[ctx.self.state.item] = (player.state.bag[ctx.self.state.item] ?? 0) + 1; ctx.destroy(ctx.self.id); } // scripts/db.js export async function migrate(sql) { await sql`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS best (user_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, score INTEGER NOT NULL)`; await sql`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS best_score ON best (score)`; } // the match's end: their summary row await ctx.sql`INSERT INTO best VALUES (@caller, ${name}, ${score}) ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET name = excluded.name, score = MAX(score, excluded.score)`; // the board; the HUD renders state, never SQL ctx.world.state.allTime = (await ctx.sql`SELECT name, score FROM best ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10`).rows;
A board also goes to Spawn's game page: each player's number in player.state (their best, their total), named under world.config.yaml leaderboards (spawn api LeaderboardDef).

SQL runs at an event, never per tick: onArrive/onLeave (the player's machine), a player's behavior, a cron, run_script, db.js. A hook's or behavior's call publishes with the save and runs as its player; one the save lacks answers statement_not_published.

A save in onLeave lands however the player left: their machine runs it at the door; when their tab dies, Spawn's machine there runs it from the last state everyone saw, @caller bound to them; alone with no Spawn machine there, nobody does: a game that must survive that also writes at its moment. Keep onLeave one fast call.

platformState: ["gold", "inventory"] on the player template makes these keys cheat-proof in a multiplayer world, one player's room too: no player's machine writes them, sim.js's onArrive included; yours and the creator's do. Start them in its state.

simulatedBy: "platform" on a row (a bank, a bot director; at spawn or live) runs on Spawn's machine, never a player's, even with nobody near. = null undials; it stops in an empty place. It can move machines: a finished onSpawn's writes are not repeated, ctx.self.session starts with what onSpawn left. Players who see it still write and destroy it. Keep no module state.

A thing one player alone sees: visibility: "owner" on a row under them (a hand: spawn({ parent: player.id, visibility: "owner", … })) reaches their screen, live, at a join and in the saved world; visibility: "platform" (a deck), or "owner" with no player above, reaches no player. Both reach the platform, you and the creator; a platform row's ctx.random() draws the platform's entropy, never the world's seed. The platform deals: it writes the deck and the hands. Any other row or emit, audience: { player: id } included, can reach others: a secret rides a row with the word. The owner's HUD reads it by ctx.getObject(id), null elsewhere.

Crons: engine.crons: [{ schedule: "/5 * * *", script: "crons/respawn.js" }] in world.config.yaml; the file exports async function cron(ctx); a minute the finest step. A one-shot is ctx.after. Crons, timers and sim.js run while someone is in; with nobody in: routing.alwaysOn →rooms-and-matchmaking.

A talking, seeing, hearing character: ctx.job("llm:chat", { conversationId, system, message, media, maxHistory (20), model: "fast" | "smart" (Spawn's models; smart: slower, stronger) | an OpenRouter id (20 asks a player an hour) }, (r) => …) → r.data.text; a fourth { onPart: (p) => … } streams it: p.text the next words, p.first a restart; "llm:generate" with schema → r.data.object; "llm:clear" forgets. media: […], that turn alone: a /cdn/… address or a data: URL. conversationId IS the memory: "npc:" + npcId + ":" + playerId per player. r: { ok, data, error: { message, code, retryAfterMs } }, never thrown; seconds pass: state.loading from submit to callback.

ctx.job("llm:chat", { conversationId, system, message, media, maxHistory (20), model: "fast" | "smart" (Spawn's models; smart: slower, stronger) | an OpenRouter id (20 asks a player an hour) }, (r) => …)
r: { ok, data, error: { message, code, retryAfterMs } }

Words a player writes that others read (a pet's name, a board post): ctx.job("text:check", { text }, (r) => …) runs any length through chat's filter, posting nothing; r.data.ok false: show your own words. chat:send posts and checks nothing.

The outside web (a webhook): a job runs where it is asked: from a player's body, on their device. fetch(url, { method: "POST", body }) in its run reaches any public address but Spawn's own hosts. A picture or a picture-free .glb POSTed to "/cdn/" with its content-type by a builder or Spawn's machine stores once; clients load its location like an upload. A feed holds new WebSocket(url) in an async function* run yielding each message to the asker's onPart; ask it once from sim.js, again when it ends. A behavior or sim.js on Spawn's machine reaches no outside address. To prove the player to a service, ctx.job("player:token", {}, (r) => …) from their body answers r.data.token, a signed JWT (sub = player.userId) verified at https://www.spawn.co/api/.well-known/jwks.json.
Names of players who left, by id: "player:names" from the owner's body (spawn api job).

ctx.notifyDm(message, { to: player, link: "+garden" }) rings their Spawn bell and phone, playing or away, not Savi's chat: to a player row or its userId, link where it opens this world: a place, or a room as "world:" + ctx.world.id + "/room:" + name + "+garden". Only this world's players get it (a waitlist is Spawn's: spawn publish propose_covers --opensAt). A line holds 1,000 characters; a world sends a player at most 5 a UTC day, grouped and held through their night; players can mute it; a line not sent says why in getLogs. Send the moments worth coming back for, one each; notifyDmOnce takes { to } too.

ctx.sql`…`: { rows, changes, lastInsertRowid } // ${v} binds string · number · boolean · null (JSON.stringify a structure; json_each reads it), never concatenate; a call from a player's machine is a round trip: a list is one call; semicolons = ordered statements in one transaction; rows [] = none, changes 0 = a guarded write refused; errors throw into getLogs; calls queue one at a time and each answers, however slow: never time one out, resend it or read it back budgets: ≤ 100 parameters a statement, ≤ 5 SELECTs joined by UNION / UNION ALL / INTERSECT / EXCEPT (one multi-row VALUES (…), (…) seeds rows, uncapped) // LIMIT big scans @caller // the player this call acts for: a player's hook or behavior, singleplayer, where a sim.js, cron or place-hook write binds it alone, else `statement_not_player_invocable`; run_script, db.js and a multiplayer cron or place hook have none: bind ${playerId} scripts/db.js: export async function migrate(sql) // before the first statement: idempotent DDL and set-based backfills; a throw never blocks play: the prior schema serves and it re-runs at the next spec version dev and live are two databases // the schema carries to live on its first call, rows do not: seed live with INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in migrate() money says its domain in SQL: WHERE coins >= ${amount} AND ${amount} > 0, the credit gated on the debit's changes // a negative amount pays the sender otherwise
